Although he is not an acquaintance from our earlier days he has proved entirely reliable. Naturally, in spite of that, we remain very cautious. We have so often dissuaded our friends from risking a desired contact, that it is now up to their initiative to use, or discard, the possibilities which we report to them. The Intermediary agreed with us and understands he possibilities fully. He said also that his circle's present method of working was to take jobs in places - for instance, Hitler's police administration etc. - either where they had the best chance of gleaning information that might be useful to us, or in places where, when the situation has developed a bit, they might be effective. They consider the time not yet ripe for leaflets, sabotage etc. We are considering a workers' association for when he comes again, in which outstanding representatives from every group should take part. Future tasks for the Leftists would be discussed, above all the tasks for those inside over there, both present and future. The purposes would be to indicate certain correct lines for him and his friends to work on: to clarify opinions and bring as many as possible of the different groups of anti-Hitlerites under one leadership. If you have any suggestions let us have them - as far as possible without mentioning concrete methods - simply your ideas of such tasks, for to-day and to-morrow. You well know the uneasiness over here about Neutrality and fear of the Communists. Besides one never knows when they will start to read the mail.

Some prisoners of war who have recently escaped told us very nice stories about their experiences with German labourers with whom they worked in secret at the factory. One man travelled 150 km to a large town in order to get hold of a compass for a prisoner, who made very effective use of it in his flight. When a compass cannot be procured the workmen manufacture one by primitive means at their disposal where they work. One of them told a touching story of his leave-taking from a comrade at work: "Au revoir mein Freund!" And he wrote down the complicated French address so that he should be able to come over and celebrate Hitler's downfall together. - But, of course, all this goes on in secret and with great caution. Open opposition dares not show itself yet.

M.G.B...31st Oct. 1941.
